subject: Clarify cloud scope, subprocessors, and bridge letter availability for SOC 2
messages:
From: Alice Murray <alice.murray@enterpriseco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 / cloud scope questions + bridge letter request

Hi Camila,

Thanks for taking this — our procurement and security teams are reviewing Redwood for a pilot and asked for a few clarifications before we proceed to legal. We have three specific asks:

1) Can you confirm the dates covered by Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II (we need the exact audit window and the report PDF)?
2) For cloud infrastructure (we run on AWS), does Redwood consider the cloud provider report a carve-out or a carve-in for controls like: encryption key management, logging/monitoring, and backups? Our security policy requires an explicit mapping.
3) If the Redwood SOC 2 audit window does not fully overlap our procurement schedule, can you provide a bridge letter or interim attestation covering the gap?

I've attached our security questionnaire (high level) — the sections we care most about are: data encryption, logging retention, subprocessors, and vendor incident notification timelines. Also: can you provide a list of subprocessors used in the last 12 months?

Appreciate a quick read — our deadlines are tight (we'd like to close procurement by 2026-06-15).

Thanks,
Alice Murray
InfoSec PM, EnterpriseCo
alice.murray@enterpriseco.com

Attachment: SecurityQuestionnaire-EnterpriseCo.pdf (1.2MB, PDF)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Murray <alice.murray@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / cloud scope questions + bridge letter request

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dylan (Head of Security) and Marissa (Legal/Privacy) to make sure we cover audit specifics and procurement language.

Quick answers up front:
- We can share the SOC 2 Type II report PDF and a one-page summary today and confirm the exact audit window. See link: https://drive.redwood.com/soc2/summary (PDF attached).
- For most cloud infrastructure controls we treat the cloud provider's SOC as a carve-out for infrastructure responsibilities (compute, physical data center controls). Control ownership above that layer (service config, application-level encryption, data access logging) is within Redwood's scope. We can produce a subservice mapping that aligns specific control families (e.g., CC6, CC7) to either Redwood or the cloud provider.
- Bridge letter: yes, we routinely provide a bridge letter to covered customers that documents the last audit period and attests there have been no material changes to controls since the report period. We'll confirm exact language and timeline.

Action items for us:
1) Dylan will send the formal audit window dates, the SOC PDF, and a suggested bridge letter draft.
2) Marissa can confirm any contract language you should expect for subprocessors and will provide the most recent subprocessors list.
3) Camila (that's me) will put together the subservice mapping focused on your encryption, logging, and backup questions and return by EOD tomorrow (2026-05-12).

If you have a preferred format for the subservice mapping (spreadsheet vs table in PDF) let me know; we typically send a CSV that maps control families to vendor and evidence references.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf (300KB, PDF)

From: Alice Murray <alice.murray@enterpriseco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / cloud scope questions + bridge letter request

Camila — thanks, that helps. A couple follow-ups from procurement/security:

- For encryption: we need to know whether customer-controlled keys (KMS) are in-scope or if Redwood uses cloud-managed keys. If you use KMS, which party manages CMKs?
- For logging: confirm retention periods for audit logs (IAM, admin actions, data access) and whether those logs are stored in a system that is covered by Redwood SOC 2 controls or by the cloud provider's report.
- For backups: what is the backup retention policy and is backup integrity tested?
- Subprocessors: please provide a full name and jurisdiction for each subprocessors used in the last 12 months.

We're attaching our procurement checklist — some of these items are non-negotiable or will need contract-level SLR language (e.g., incident notification <24 hours). If the SOC report doesn't show sufficient coverage we may request additional attestations.

We can be flexible on format. A CSV mapping would be ideal for our intake team. If you could also include the SOC2 audit window in the PDF (or the bridge letter) that would be great.

Thanks again,
Alice

Attachment: Procurement-Checklist.pdf (450KB, PDF)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alice Murray <alice.murray@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / cloud scope questions + bridge letter request

Hi Alice — thanks for the detailed asks. Below are consolidated answers and attachments. Marissa, feel free to jump in for contract language.

1) SOC 2 audit window and report
- Audit period covered by the most recent SOC 2 Type II: 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30.
- We're attaching the full report (redwood_soc2_typeii_20260101-20260630.pdf) to this thread and have also shared a short summary at: https://drive.redwood.com/soc2/summary

2) Cloud provider (AWS) treatment: carve-out vs carve-in
- Infrastructure layer (physical security, hypervisor, networking, underlying host OS) — we treat AWS SOC reports as carve-out (i.e., AWS controls cover those responsibilities).
- Service/application layer (Redwood-managed KMS keys, application-level encryption, user access controls, application logging) — these are in-scope for Redwood and are tested in our SOC report.
- We will provide a CSV subservice mapping that enumerates control families and indicates "Redwood" or "AWS" as the primary responsible party; that CSV will also include evidence references where applicable.

3) Encryption / KMS
- Redwood uses AWS KMS for envelope encryption. Customer data encryption at rest is managed by Redwood; we manage CMKs that are tenant-segregated for production workloads. If a customer requires BYOK (bring your own key), we support a contract-enabled workflow and can describe responsibilities and evidence for that configuration.

4) Logging retention and location
- Audit logs (admin actions, IAM changes, deploy events) are retained for 13 months by default in our central logging cluster (hosted on AWS; logging collector is within Redwood's control plane and included in our SOC scope). Application-level access logs are retained 13 months; security event logs are retained 25 months for enterprise customers on request (we can add contract language).

5) Backups and integrity
- Backups are incremental daily with a 90-day retention by default; critical data snapshots are retained 365 days. Backup restore procedures and periodic integrity tests are part of our change control and backup policies (we can provide the runbook excerpt as evidence).

6) Subprocessors (last 12 months) — name and jurisdiction
- Amazon Web Services, Inc. (us-east-1, us)
- FastObject Storage, Inc. (S3-compatible backup provider) (us)
- CloudDB Partners (managed DB ops) (us)
- Stripe, Inc. (payments) (US)
- SentryOps Ltd (error monitoring) (IE)
- MailRelay Co. (email deliverability) (US)

(Full CSV attached with contract jurisdictions and data access descriptions.)

7) Bridge letter
- We can issue a bridge letter that references the report above and attests to the control environment between 2026-07-01 and the next audit period. Draft attached; we can tailor language to match your procurement team's requirements.

8) Evidence delivery and format
- We'll provide: the SOC 2 PDF, the CSV subservice mapping, the subprocessors CSV, and a bridge letter draft. If you need an auditor-to-auditor exchange, we can provide contact details for our auditor (Bob Jensen at AuditFirm) under an NDA — Bob is CC'd here.

Next steps:
- Camila will upload the subservice mapping CSV and subprocessors CSV by EOD today.
- Marissa will prepare suggested contract language around incident notification and BYOK options and send it to you.
- If this looks good, we'll produce a final bridge letter and the requested attachments.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_soc2_typeii_20260101-20260630.pdf (7.8MB, PDF); subservice_mapping.csv (27KB); subprocessors_202605.csv (12KB); bridge_letter_draft.docx (24KB)
